body: Nikola listed via SPAC (VectoIQ) in Jun 2020 and within days reached an intraday ~$94 (~$30 bn market cap, above Ford) with essentially no revenue. On 10 Sep 2020 Hindenburg's 'Ocean of Lies' report showed, among other things, that the 2018 'Nikola One in motion' video was a truck rolling downhill, and that claimed in-house components were bought from suppliers. Founder Trevor Milton resigned on 20 Sep; the GM partnership was scaled back; Milton was convicted of securities and wire fraud (Oct 2022) and sentenced to 4 years (Dec 2023) -- later pardoned (2025). Nikola filed Chapter 11 in Feb 2025 after burning billions; equity ~0 (after a 1:30 reverse split in 2024). Visible flags: (1) pre-revenue company valued above incumbents; (2) founder making unverifiable technical claims on social media/podcasts; (3) SPAC structure with limited diligence and insider/sponsor lock-up expiries; (4) partnerships announced as validation (GM, CNH/Iveco) with equity-for-tech structures; (5) Hindenburg's work was checkable from public sources and ex-employees. Lesson: SPAC-era pre-revenue stories have terrible base rates; founder credibility can be tested with scuttlebutt; a single falsified claim usually means more.

data.early_signals: pre-revenue mega-cap; founder claims; SPAC; partnership 'validation'

title: Nikola (2020-2025): pre-revenue SPAC hype
